EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours witnessed a critical breakdown in US-Iran diplomatic efforts, with President Trump emphatically rejecting Iran's latest peace proposal as "unacceptable" and threatening renewed military action, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, the conflict on the Israel-Lebanon border escalated significantly following a Hezbollah drone attack that killed an Israeli reservist, alongside ongoing cross-border strikes and mutual threats, signaling a high risk of broader regional military engagement.

IRAN
Iran formally rejected the US peace proposal, labeling it "unacceptable" as it reportedly demanded "surrender to Trump's excessive demands" and did not include US compensation for war damages. Iran's counter-proposal, mediated by Pakistan, outlined demands for an end to the naval blockade, full lifting of US sanctions, release of frozen funds, a definitive ceasefire in Lebanon (termed a "red line"), Iranian management of the Strait of Hormuz, and a 30-day post-ceasefire negotiation period for nuclear issues. Crucially, Iran's proposal explicitly did not include agreement to remove enriched uranium from the country or dismantle nuclear facilities, despite earlier US claims of such an agreement. Instead, Iran offered to dilute some enriched uranium and transfer highly enriched material to a third country, with a provision for its return if talks fail. Iran's Atomic Energy Organization Head, Mohammad Eslami, reiterated that uranium enrichment is not negotiable and activities remain peaceful.

On the military front, air defense systems in southwest Iran reportedly shot down an "enemy" reconnaissance drone. Similar activity, involving "multiple drones" and active anti-air defenses, was reported in Andimeshk and northern Dezful, with claims of an "enemy aircraft" downed. Explosions in Shiraz and Daylam were attributed to controlled detonations of unexploded ordnance. Infrastructure-wise, reconstruction work is underway on the B1 Bridge in Karaj, which was damaged during the US-Israeli war. Iran executed Erfan Shakoorzadeh, 29, an aeronautical engineer, for allegedly spying for the Mossad and CIA, though Iran Human Rights Society claims a forced confession.

Economically, the Minister of Communications stated that internet restrictions are due to "wartime conditions," with reports indicating a two-month-long internet shutdown causing significant economic damage and exacerbating a "digital divide" through "Internet Pro" services. Fuel shortages were reported in Isfahan and Kermanshah, prompting a government plan for fuel management without price increases starting May 21. Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad refuted US claims of a major decline in the country’s oil production due to the naval blockade.

Politically, Supreme Leader advisor Ali Akbar Velayati warned Trump against exploiting Iran's "restraint" and asserted Iran's victory on the battlefield. President Pezeshkian thanked Iraq's Grand Ayatollah Sistani for his support. IRGC Commander Mohammad Ali Jafari stated that no further negotiations would occur without an end to the war, lifting of sanctions, release of frozen funds, war reparations, and recognition of Iran's sovereignty over Hormuz. The Secretary of the Supreme Council of Cultural Revolution advocated for moving military targets away from residential areas.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical point of contention; MarineTraffic reported only 9 container ships passed through in the last 60 days, with 42 still stuck. A Qatari tanker was reportedly stopped and turned back by Iran, and the passage of an Emirati LPG tanker is pending Iranian permission. Iran's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee warned against an "UAE-Israel axis" in the region.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the razing of four Hamas tunnels in the southern Gaza Strip, totaling 4km, one of which was reportedly used to hold hostages. In the West Bank, an armed individual who opened fire at forces at the Qalandiya crossing was neutralized, and a military court convicted Nadmi Abu Bakar for the intentional killing of Sgt. Amit Ben Yigal in 2020.

Tragically, Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, 47, a driver from Petah Tikva, was killed on May 10 by a Hezbollah explosive drone near the Lebanon border. This marks the fourth security force member killed by drones during the current ceasefire period. On the home front, sirens sounded in Neve Yam (Carmel region) due to an interceptor missile launched towards a Hezbollah surface-to-air missile targeting an IAF drone. Items of unexploded ordnance (AMAL) were found on Tel Aviv's northern Cliff Beach, leading to a temporary closure by police.

Politically, PM Netanyahu strongly defended the appointment of Maj. Gen. Roman Gofman as Mossad head, rebuking Mossad chief Barnea for a letter to the Attorney General regarding the appointment and dismissing concerns over Gofman's past conduct. Netanyahu convened a security discussion following Iran's rejection of the US proposal. The Knesset approved an extension of reserve duty call-up until May 31, allowing up to 400,000 reservists. Netanyahu stated that "the war is not over" and expressed belief that the fall of the Iranian regime would lead to the end of Hezbollah, Hamas, and the Houthis. He also claimed plans to phase out US financial aid to Israel within a decade and accused China of supplying components for Iranian missiles. In response to EU sanctions on Israeli settlers, Finance Minister Smotrich demanded the transfer of strategic areas in Judea and Samaria from A and B zones to Area C, calling it a "de facto cancellation of the Oslo Accords." Shomron Regional Council head Yossi Dagan condemned the EU sanctions as "ignorance and anti-Israeli," while the Peace Now Movement welcomed them.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, IDF forces razed four Hamas tunnels in the southern Strip, including one previously used for holding hostages. A classified Israeli document indicated that Hamas is actively regrouping, collecting intelligence on IDF forces, recruiting dozens of fighters, producing hundreds of explosives, mortars, and anti-tank rockets monthly, and conducting training while improving existing infrastructure. The humanitarian situation in Gaza continues to raise concerns, with reports highlighting risks to media workers and children growing up amid violence.

In the West Bank, an armed individual was neutralized after opening fire on forces at the Qalandiya crossing. The EU formally approved sanctions against three Israeli individuals and four organizations identified as involved in violent settler activity and supporting extreme settlements, including Nahala, Amana, Hashomer Yosh, Regavim, and activist Daniella Weiss. This move was met with strong condemnation from Israeli officials and welcomed by Israeli peace groups.

LEBANON
Hezbollah escalated its operations against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, launching multiple rockets and explosive drones. One such drone attack on May 10 killed Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, an Israeli reservist. Separately, three IDF soldiers were lightly injured in another explosive drone attack, and two explosive drones damaged unmanned engineering vehicles. Hezbollah also fired a surface-to-air missile at an Israeli Air Force drone, which was intercepted. Automated phone calls were reportedly made to Kiryat Shmona settlers, issuing evacuation orders and threats. Hezbollah also claimed targeting Merkava tanks and bulldozers with drones.

In response, Israeli forces conducted strikes in southern Lebanon. An IAF strike on a building killed two Hezbollah operatives near Israeli ground forces. The IDF also targeted a rocket launcher on a truck that had fired at Israeli forces. Israeli strikes were reported in al-Duwair, al-Rihan, Kafr Fila, Jarjouaa, Zawtar al-Gharbiya, with one martyr and four injured in Abba. An IAF helicopter evacuating wounded soldiers from southern Lebanon experienced a technical malfunction, forcing it to land, but was later fixed and departed safely; it was not hit by enemy fire. Two Israeli soldiers were sentenced to military jail (21 and 14 days) for desecrating a Virgin Mary statue in the Christian village of Debel. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called on the US to pressure Israel to halt its ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iraqi-Iranian Supreme Security Committee met in Baghdad, emphasizing the importance of enhancing joint security coordination and tightening border controls to prevent infiltration by terrorist or armed groups threatening regional stability. Conflicting reports emerged regarding the presence of an American-Israeli base in western Iraq, with a member of the Badr parliamentary faction confirming its existence and claiming Iraqi security forces were denied access. US espionage flights were reported near this alleged Israeli base in Al-Nakheeb. In Syria, four individuals from "Joulani gangs" were killed in Hasakah following an attack by ISIS on their bus. The Syrian transitional government under Al-Jolani adjusted its cabinet, removing several ministers, reportedly to build public trust or to align more closely with Russia.

GULF STATES
The Kuwaiti Army reported intercepting "a number of hostile drones" in its airspace on May 10, with the origin remaining unspecified. Saudi Arabian Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan engaged in a phone conversation with his Pakistani counterpart, discussing the regional situation and efforts to de-escalate tensions, particularly concerning Iran-US interactions and the importance of maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. Oman's Foreign Minister, Badr Al Busaidi, called for a humanitarian initiative to address "stranded" ships in the Gulf, in cooperation with littoral states. Former Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani stated that Iran would emerge "stronger" politically and militarily after the current conflict. Reports from Bahrain indicated clashes between citizens and authorities, protesting the revocation of citizenships and arrests of Shiite clerics accused of supporting Iran.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Rejects Iranian Proposal:** President Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable," "stupid," and a "piece of garbage," and indicated he is considering renewed military options against Iran, including "Project Freedom" for the Strait of Hormuz.
2.  **Iranian Counter-Proposal:** Iran's proposal demanded an end to the naval blockade, lifting of US sanctions, release of frozen funds, an immediate ceasefire in Lebanon (a "red line"), Iranian management of the Strait of Hormuz, and 30 days of post-war negotiations for nuclear issues, but notably excluded agreement to remove enriched uranium or dismantle facilities.
3.  **Israeli Reservist Killed in Lebanon:** Warrant Officer (res.) Alexander Glovanyov, 47, was killed on May 10 by a Hezbollah explosive drone near the Lebanon border, marking a significant escalation and the fourth Israeli security force fatality from drones during the ceasefire.
4.  **EU Sanctions Israeli Settlers:** The European Union approved sanctions against three Israeli individuals and four organizations (Nahala, Amana, Hashomer Yosh, Regavim, and Daniella Weiss) for violent activities and support of extreme settlements in the West Bank, prompting a strong response from Israel.
5.  **Hezbollah Drone and Rocket Barrages:** Hezbollah launched multiple rockets and explosive drones at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, damaging unmanned engineering vehicles and injuring three IDF soldiers, while also firing a surface-to-air missile at an IAF drone.
6.  **Iranian Spy Execution:** Iran executed Erfan Shakoorzadeh, 29, an aeronautical engineer, convicted of spying for the Mossad and CIA, according to state media.
7.  **Strait of Hormuz Blockade Impact:** MarineTraffic reported only 9 container ships transited Hormuz in the last 60 days, with 42 stuck, leading a UN official to warn of a potential humanitarian crisis if fertilizer transit is not allowed. A Qatari tanker was turned back by Iran, and an Emirati tanker's passage is pending.
8.  **Hamas Regrouping in Gaza:** A classified Israeli document indicates Hamas is actively regrouping in Gaza, recruiting fighters, producing weapons (explosives, rockets, anti-tank missiles), and conducting training despite IDF presence, while improving existing infrastructure.
9.  **US Military Posturing:** Reports of US refueling aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport and an Ohio-class submarine entering the Mediterranean suggest increased US military presence and readiness in the region, coinciding with Trump's threats of military action against Iran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following the complete breakdown of US-Iran diplomatic efforts and President Trump's explicit threats of renewed, severe military action against Iran, including the military reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Netanyahu's reiteration that "the war is not over" further amplifies this risk. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran continues its blockade and the US threatens intervention, and the Israel-Lebanon border, characterized by daily, increasingly lethal exchanges from Hezbollah and Israeli retaliatory strikes. The killing of an IDF reservist by a Hezbollah drone is a significant escalation from a "ceasefire" posture. Iran's steadfast refusal to negotiate uranium enrichment and the US demand for its removal from Iranian facilities also create a high-stakes standoff. Military posture changes include increased US force projection in the region (refueling aircraft, Ohio-class submarine), and Trump's consideration of striking unhit Iranian targets. Red lines include Iran's non-negotiable enrichment program and its declaration of a ceasefire in Lebanon as a condition for broader negotiations. The ongoing rearmament and training of Hamas in Gaza also pose a significant latent threat on Israel's southern front.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture, articulated by President Trump, is one of deep frustration and consideration of military options against Iran, potentially after his upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The White House, however, indicated no rush for talks. Trump criticized high gasoline prices in the US, attributing them to the conflict.
Gulf states like Kuwait reported drone interceptions, and Saudi Arabia engaged with Pakistan on de-escalation efforts, particularly concerning Iran-US talks and maritime security in Hormuz. Oman called for humanitarian initiatives for stranded ships.
The European Union approved sanctions against violent Israeli settlers and Hamas figures, with some EU foreign ministers offering to leverage their experience for Iran-US talks. The UK imposed sanctions on 12 Iranian individuals and entities, with PM Starmer stating Britain would not be drawn into the Iran war. France ruled out unilateral military deployment in Hormuz without Iranian coordination, emphasizing defensive operations.
Russia's envoy to international organizations, Ulyano, stated that US demands to destroy Iran's nuclear facilities contradict the NPT. China opposed US sanctions on its firms for alleged aid to Iran, calling them "illegal," ahead of Trump's visit to Beijing where Iran will be a key discussion point.
Pakistan continued its mediation efforts between the US and Iran, seeking a "memorandum of understanding" to de-escalate and open broader dialogue. India's PM Modi warned of risks from the Iran war, urging citizens to reduce fuel consumption and avoid foreign travel. Kazakhstan expressed readiness to help resolve the Iranian nuclear issue. UN Secretary-General Guterres urged de-escalation in Hormuz and continued talks.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions exist, most notably between Trump's claim that Iran initially agreed to remove enriched uranium and explicit Iranian denials. The impact of the naval blockade on Iran's oil production also remains disputed. Unverified claims include the existence and nature of a purported American-Israeli base in western Iraq, and specific anonymous reports regarding Hezbollah's automated evacuation calls to Kiryat Shmona settlers and alleged targets for a future Israeli attack. Propaganda indicators are prevalent across all involved parties, with Iranian state media portraying a victorious stance, Trump employing highly inflammatory rhetoric, and an anti-regime Iranian channel celebrating Israeli military actions. Reporting gaps include a lack of detail on specific unexploded ordnance found on Tel Aviv beaches, and the precise context of "Joulani gangs" activity in Syria. The reliability of information varies, with direct official statements and military announcements considered high-confidence, while anonymous sources, opinion pieces, and speculative predictions carry lower confidence.
